gene_info.description: Hemoglobin subunit beta â€” oxygen transport

impact.description: A single nucleotide change alters one amino acid in the protein sequence. Depending on the physicochemical properties of the substitution and the residue's structural role, this may disrupt protein folding, binding, or enzymatic activity.

interpretation.impact_meaning: A single nucleotide change alters one amino acid in the protein sequence. Depending on the physicochemical properties of the substitution and the residue's structural role, this may disrupt protein folding, binding, or enzymatic activity.
interpretation.general_summary: Variant rs334 (NM_000518.5:c.20A>T) introduces a transversion in HBB, resulting in a missense variant (p.Glu7Val). The global alternate allele frequency is 0.0010 (0.10%). It participates in the Hemoglobin synthesis / Oxygen transport pathway.

genecards.gene_summary: Hemoglobin subunit beta â€” oxygen transport

impact_explanation.meaning: Predicted to alter protein sequence or function without complete disruption.
biological_consequences: Single amino acid substitution (may affect folding or binding)
Changed enzymatic activity or substrate specificity
impact_explanation.interpretation: MODERATE impact variants change the protein but do not destroy it. The actual effect ranges from benign (tolerated substitution in a non-critical region) to damaging (substitution at an active site or conserved residue). Computational tools like SIFT and PolyPhen-2 help distinguish tolerated from deleterious changes, but functional studies provide the strongest evidence.

significance_explanation.definition: The variant has been determined to cause disease based on strong evidence from multiple independent sources.
significance_explanation.interpretation: Pathogenic variants are considered causative for the associated condition. In clinical settings, a Pathogenic classification typically triggers diagnostic confirmation, cascade family testing, and disease-specific management. This is the highest-confidence classification for disease-causing variants.
evidence_basis: ClinVar expert panel or practice guideline review
Segregation with disease in multiple affected families
Absence or extremely low frequency in population databases (gnomAD)
Published case-level evidence in peer-reviewed literature
